title: Visibility-Aware Texture Consensus and Local Structural Constraints for 3D Gaussian Reconstruction in Texture- Degraded Scenes
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) can propagate unreliable photometric residuals into geometric parameters in weakly textured, repetitive-texture, low-light, and occlusion-boundary regions. We investigate Visibility-Aware Texture Consensus (VTC), parameter-level loss routing, and local-PCA structural constraints for texture-degraded reconstruction. Under a strict 80/20 path-isolated protocol on four NeRF Synthetic scenes, the simplified configuration improves the official-validation macro-average by 0.0661 dB in PSNR, 0.00246 in SSIM, 0.00136 in Alpha IoU, and reduces LPIPS by 0.00036 and Outside alpha by 6.33×10 − 5 relative to Control. In an additional four-scene, five-seed paired matrix at 300 iterations, PSNR improves for all five seeds in every scene; the exact two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test gives p = 0.0625. Controllable texture removal, illumination reduction, and occlusion experiments show monotonic changes in degradation proxies, supporting the proposed identifiability analysis. Additional DTU and Mip-NeRF 360 experiments verify cross-dataset interfaces, while standard-densification tests delimit transfer behavior. Overall, the evidence supports improved relative robustness under a low-budget fixed-Gaussian protocol, while not supporting state-of-the-art claims on real-world data or performance gains from consensus inheritance.
